Commercial production of bio-diesel    
*112. SHRI R.P. GOENKA: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any detailed studies have been undertaken to explore 
the possibility of commercial production of bio-diesel, derived from certain 
plants like 'Jatropha', 'Pungam' etc. which can be grown even in 
wastelands, for use as alternative fu el to petro-diesel like LNG, CNG 
etc.; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that a number of other countries like Canada, 
the US and some European countries have already undertaken major 
bio-diesel programmes to identify a nd develop high yielding varieties of 
plants and also for its use in transport vehicles etc.; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI 
MANI SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) to (d) Bio-dies el, a diesel fuel substitute, is 
made from vegetable oils (both edible & non-edible) and animal fats. 
Studies have been undertaken to explore the possibiity of production of 
bio-diesel from non-edible oils like Jatropha curcas and Pongomia. The 
Ministry of Rural Development has been made the nodal Ministry to 
implement the National mission on Bio-diesel, and that Ministry has 
informed that a detailed project report is being prepared by The Energy 
Research Institute (TARI) for the purpose. 
At present, field trials are being conducted by oil marketing 
companies to use bio-diesel and diesel blend on buses in collaboration 
with Haryana Roadways and with Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and 
Transport Undertaking (BEST), Mumbai. Field trials and engine tests on 
locomotives are also in progress. If the field trials establish the efficacy 
14 

[13 July, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
of bio-diesel and diesel blend, and indicate the possibility of economic 
pricing of these products, then large scale oil seeds plantation would 
have to be undertaken before commercial production of bio-diesel begins. 
The Government is aware that the European Union (EU), United 
States of America (USA), Canada and some other countries have 
undertaken bio-diesel programmes, with a variety of feed-stocks being 
used. However, the feed-stocks for production of bio-diesel in EU and 
USA are vegetable oils which are mainly edible oils. In USA, the bio- 
diesel programme is based on soyabean oil while in EU and most of 
Europe, sunflower oil and rapeseed o il are the major feed-stocks. Bio- 
diesel is being blended at 5 to 20% levels in USA, Canada and the EU, 
and is being used commercially. India is short of edible oil, hence non- 
edible oils like Jatropha curcas and Pongomia are proposed for bio-diesel 
production.

Appreciation of Rupee 
275. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA RAO: Will the Minister of FINANCE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the exporting community is putting 
pressure on the RBI to arrest the appr eciation of Rupee as it is creating 
problems for exporters; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that due to appreciation of Rupee, 
according to the NCAER,  the overall export pe rformance decelerated 
from 20.8 per cent in April—December 2002 to 14.4 per cent in the 
corresponding period of 2003; and 
(c) if so, what steps the RBI is taking in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) to (c) During 2003-04, the Rupee 
appreciated by 5.3 per cent agaisnt the US Dollar on an annual average 
basis. At the same time, it depreci ated against the currencies of major 
non-dollar trading partners of India. In its Quarterly Review of the Economy 
published in April 2004, the NCAER observed that in US Dollar terms exports 
showed a lower growth of 14.4 per cent in April—December, 2003 compared 
to 0.8 per cent in April—December 2002. It also pointed to the appreciation 
of the Rupee against the US Dollar as a factor causing a dent in India's 
exports. The scenario has since changed. According to the latest figures, 
export growth for 2003-04 at 17.3 per cent was not significantly lower than 
20.3 per cent achieved in 2002-03. It is therefore evident that the movements 
in the Rupee value were smooth and orderly, avoiding undue adjustment 
costs. The management of the Indian Rupee continues to be broadly 
market-based with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervening only in the 
event of smoothening excessive volatilities in the foreign exchange market.

279. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Forex inflow has been continuing thus 
inflating Forex reserve; 
(b) if so, whether Government have arrived at a safe and optimal 
level to keep the Forex reserves a nd utilise the balance for repaying the 
foreign debt; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) Yes, Sir. Substantial foreign 
exchange inflows during the last two years have led to a large accretion 
of foreign exchange reserves. 
(b) There are no commonly acceptable yardsticks regarding the 
optimal level of reserves. Existing yardsticks like import cover, short- 
term debt, and liquidity at risk, are essentially indicative in nature. Thus, 
58

the concept of optimal size of reserv es depends on various factors. With 
the changing profile of ca pital flows, the traditiona l approach of assessing 
reserve adequacy in terms of import cover has been broadened to include 
other parameters, such as the size, composition, and risk profiles of 
various types of capital flows, as well as the likely external shocks to 
which the economy is vulnerable. 
(c) The significant increase in fore x reserves enabled prepayment 
of external debt on Government account amounting to US$ 2.9 billion in 
2002-03 and US$ 3.8 billion in 2003-04.

Target of rural credit by Banks 
280. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: W ill the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that despite RBI stipulations, flow of credit to 
agriculture and other rural enterp rises from commercial banks both in 
public and private sector has been unable to achieve the annual targets 
perennially; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) the steps contemplated, if any,  by Government to ensure 
compliance of the target by the Banks; and 
(d) the steps taken, if any, for implementation of the 
recommendaiions contained in the report of the Joint Committee on 
Revitalization Support to Co-operative Credit Structure headed by 
Shri Balasaheb Vikhe Patil as the then Union Minister of State for Finance? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) a nd (b) A target of 18 per cent of 
Net Bank Credit has been stipulated for lending to agriculture under 
priority sector lending by domestic scheduled commercial Banks, both 
in the public and private sector. However, no target has been stipulated 
for lending to other rural enterprises by domestic Scheduled Commercial 
Banks. As reported by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) credit to agriculture 
by Public Sector Banks and Private Sector Banks has increased in 
absolute terms from Rs. 73,507 crore (15.3% of Net Bank Credit) and 
Rs. 11,873 crore (10.8 per cent of Net Bank Credit) respectively as on 
59 

RAJYA SABHA [13 July, 2004] 
31st March, 2003 to Rs. 85,782 crore (15.45% of Net Bank Credit) and 
Rs. 16,370 crore (12.25 per cent of Net Bank Credit) as on 31st March, 
2004. The main reasons for the shortfall in agricultural credit as a 
percentage of NBC are:  
(i) Bank credit to other sectors growing at a faster rate; 
(ii) Drought situation in some parts of the country; 
(iii) Crash in prices of some agricultural commodities adversely 
affecting the credit off-take in agriculture; 
(iv) Low capital formation in agriculture resulting in poor credit 
absorption capacity in many areas; 
(v) Write-off of non-performing loans leading to reduction in the 
outstanding advances in the case of some banks; 
(vi) Absence of up-to-date land records in several states to 
facilitate provision of agricultural credit; and 
(vii) Inability of the small and marginal farmers to provide the 
required collateral. 
(c) RBI and National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development 
(NABARD) have taken several steps to increase the fl ow of credit to 
agriculture. These include, formulation of Special Agricultural Credit Plans 
(SACPs), opening of Specialised Agri cultural Finance Branches (SAFBs), 
implementation of the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme, introduction of 
scheme for financing agri-clinics and agri-business centres, introduction 
of scheme for financing farmers for purchase of land for agricultural 
purposes, introduction of produce marketing loans, loans for storage 
facilities, waiver of margin/security requirements, etc. Besides, during 
the current year, it is targeted to achieve a growth rate of 30% in 
disbursement of agriculture credit. 
(d) NABARD had formulated a scheme of revitalization for co- 
operative credit structure taking into account the recommendations of 
the Capoor Committee and Vikhe Patil Committee. It was proposed to 
implement the scheme after an effective regulatory framework for 
cooperative credit in stitutions has been put in place. In order to find a 
durable solution it is proposed to set up a Task Force to examine the 
reforms required in the coopera tive banking system including the 
appropriate regulatory regime. The Task force will submit its report by 
October 31, 2004.

299. SHRI A. VIAJAYA RAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of WATER

81

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

unauthorised diversion of water, if any, from the Mullaperiyar Dam? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESORUCES (SHRI JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (d) As 
reported by the Government of Tamil Nadu, there is no unauthorised 
diversion of water from the Periyar reservoir of Mullaperiyar Dam through 
Erachipalam. As per the inter-State agreement between Tamil Nadu and 
Kerala, Tamil Nadu is entitled to divert and use all the waters from the 
Periyar reservoir. Before the construction of the Hydro Power House, the 
water from Periyar reservoir was draw n through natural river course via 
Erachipalam. After the Construction of the Power House and Forebay 
dam, the water is being drawn through penstock pipes. However, 
whenever Power House is temporarily shut down, the water diverted 
through natural river course through a bye pass provided in the Forebay 
dam via, Erachipalam. The Mullaperiyar Dam is owned by the Government 
of Tamil Nadu and the maintenance of the dam is the responsibility of the 
State Government. The Government of Tamil Nadu has reported that 
there is no leakage found in the dam.

management that should govern the public enterprises, talking about the 
greatness of a Minister simply on the ground that he has not increased 
passenger fares or freight rates. But, for us, educated people, who should 
know at least the simple economics of management, to compliment the 
Minister on this criterion is, I think, a little too much to be allowed to go 
without a comment. It has now almost become an established practice

and certain sections of the Press only  on the ground that they have left 
passenger fares and the railway freight untouched. Mr. Vice-Chairman,

administration have been steadily going up. The diesel prices have gone 
up, electricity rates have gone up, maintenance charges have gone up.

effeciency in management, are complimenting the Minister because he 
has decided to follow the example of his predecessors last year or year 
before last in not touching fares and freights. Everybody else has the

SHRI URKHAO GWRA BRAHMA (Assam): Thank you 
very much, Madam, for giving me this opportunity to speak on the 
Railway Budget, 2004-05. 
At the very outset, I would like to  congratulate hon. Railway Minister, 
Shri Lalu Prasadji, for presenting his maiden Railway Budget to 
Parliament. We have been discussing this Budget during the last two or 
three days, so, I would like to raise certain points. I do not want to take 
much time of the House. I have only a few points which are very much 
concerning the people of the North-Eastern Region.

[13 July, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
Madam, it is true that our Railwa y system is the largest railway 
system in the world and is the prime mover of the nation. Apart from that, 
the most important aspec t is that the Indian Railways has connected 
every nook and corner of the nation and moulded the nation's unity and 
integrity. But it is a matter of grea t regret that, though Indian Railways 
has made a great stride in the devel opment of communication system in 
the country, it has failed to do so in the case of North-Eastern Region. In 
this Budget also no new projects to open  new Railway lines in any part of 
the region has been proposed by the Ministry. 
Madam, there was a long-standing de mand for conversion of Rangia 
to Murkongselek from Meter Gauge line to Broad Gauge. The line passes 
through five districts of Assam i.e. Kamrup, Udalguri, Sonitpur, Lakhimpur 
and Dhemaji and touches the States of Arunachal Pradesh. So, for the 
benifit of the people of Assam and Ar unachal Pradesh, the existing Meter 
Gauge line should be converted into Broad Gauge that line should be 
extended up to Itanagar, the State capi tal of Arunachal Pradesh. So, none 
of the projects undertaken by the previous Government in Assam has so 
far been completed. During the year 2004-05 the gauge conversion of 
Samuktola Road-New Bongaigaon of New Jalpaiguri-New Bongaigaon 
section has been proposed to be completed. But the gauge conversion 
from Fakirgram to Dhubri under New Jalpaiguri to New Bongaingaon 
section, which was also a sanctioned work, has not been mentioned 
clearly in the Budget. Madam, Fakirgram to Dhubri Railway line is the 
lifeline of the Kokrajhar and Dhubri di stricts of Assam. I would like to 
request the hon. Minister through you,  Madam, to start gauge conversion- 
Meter Gauge to Broad Gauge-work from Fakirgram to Dhubri with 
immediate effect. 
Madam, the present Railway recruitment policy has been a serious 
concern for some States of our count ry. Last year, during the recruitment 
of Group 'C and 'D' posts, we have witnessed some confrontation among 
the people of Bihar and Assam. T here is a demand for hundered per 
cent reservation of jobs for the local people in Group 'C and 'D'. But the 
issue has been totally ignored in the Budget and no such policy has been 
announced to settle the problem. Sir, it  is going to be a serious and lasting 
issue in future in the North Eastern Region. So, I would like to request 
hon. minister to evolve an effective policy in the Railway recruitment 
system so that hopes and aspirations of every region could be fulfilled.

Madam, I thank the hon. Minister  for his announcement that the 
upgradation work of Kokrajhar and New Bongaigaon Railway station,

connection with the model station. The h on. Minister in his Budget revealed 
the fact that the Scheduled Tribe representation in all groups of Railway 
services, except Group 'A' is less than the prescribed 7.5 per cent. In this

increased from existing 12 per cent to 15 per cent and for O.B.C. from

drive throughout the country to fill up all the backlog vacancies in respect 
of reserved vacancies for Scheduled Tribe with immediate effect. 
Madam, by not raising the passenger fares and freight charges,

you.
